From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acme-analytics.com, blueorchid-strat@example.com
Date: Tue, 21 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Slate synthesis — leadership ask & sign‑off

Team — attaching the Q2 slate decision packet for leadership review (attachment: Q2_Slate_Decision_Packet.pdf). This is the consolidated set of proposed OKRs and the condensed measurement rubric following the working sessions last week. High level ask: we need a single, executive sign‑off or explicit list of changes by EOD Thursday so the CS/RevOps teams can finalize the QBR materials for Friday’s rehearsal.

Key points in the packet:
- Three priority objectives (Customer Trust, Cost Efficiency, Serving Reliability) with proposed owner assignments and draft success criteria.
- Measurement rubric (page 7) maps metric definitions to target ranges — I've pulled a quick spreadsheet as well for easy edits.
- Fallback plan: if any objective needs de‑scoping, we propose a soft rollback that keeps the reliability initiative intact while shifting one efficiency experiment to beta.

Concrete asks:
1) Confirm the owners listed on page 2 (I put Jonas on Serving Reliability, Grace on Cost Efficiency, Kimberly on Customer Trust).
2) Approve the measurement rubric or send redlines (I attached a spreadsheet for small tweaks).
3) If you have an escalation, call out the exact metric that blocks sign‑off.

Proposed time to sync (optional): Thu 3pm PT — 30 minutes to lock decisions. I can send a calendar invite once I hear availability.

Thanks —
Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
(attachment: Q2_Slate_Decision_Packet.pdf)

Markus — quick read, thanks for pulling this together. A couple of quick notes:
- I agree with owners, but for Customer Trust we need a clearer SLA measurement (page 3 currently mixes NPS and incident MTTR). Can we split the owner‑level success criteria into two measurable bins: reliability SLO and experience NPS?
- I made small edits to the spreadsheet and attached it (measurement_rubric_v2.xlsx). See the "SLA vs Experience" tab.
- Minor ask: can we add a short paragraph on mitigation for data privacy controls in the Customer Trust objective (auditable controls + timeline)? I can draft language this afternoon.

If we can get those tweaks in place, I’m comfortable with sign‑off. Thu 3pm PT works for a short lock meeting.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
VP, Product Strategy
(attachment: measurement_rubric_v2.xlsx)

Folks — read and endorse with one caveat. Endorsement: I’m comfortable with the three objectives and the owner assignments. Caveat: the Cost Efficiency objective includes a host of experimentation signals (batching, quantization, routing) — we need to narrow to the top two experiments we'll commit budget to for Q2.

I’ve created a short doc with the narrowed experiment list and rough cost/risk matrix: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1Q2_slate_decision_packet (see "Cost_Efficiency_Experiments" section). If we prioritize two experiments today, RevOps and Eng can finalize runbooks before the QBR.

Thu 3pm PT is fine. If we lock today, I’ll prepare the QBR slide for the leadership readout and include the experiment prioritization.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Growth & Operations

Thanks for the quick review and the rubric edits — summarizing decisions and next steps so we have a single thread for the QBR packet: 

Decisions
- Owners: confirmed (Jonas: Serving Reliability; Grace: Cost Efficiency; Kimberly: Customer Trust).
- Measurement rubric: approved with Kimberly’s split of SLA vs Experience; accepted Hannah’s prioritization ask — we will commit to the top two Cost Efficiency experiments (auto‑batching and kv‑cache warmup) for Q2.
- Privacy mitigation language: Kimberly will add the suggested paragraph; draft due Wed 12pm PT.

OKRs (finalized for sign‑off):
- Objective A — Customer Trust (Owner: Kimberly Park)
  - Key Result 1: Reduce actionable incident MTTR to <45 minutes (on‑call windows measured).
  - Key Result 2: Increase enterprise NPS by 6 pts among top 30 accounts.

- Objective B — Cost Efficiency (Owner: Grace O'Connor)
  - Key Result 1: Reduce average token cost by 18% on representative production load.
  - Key Result 2: Complete 2 prioritized experiments with documented runbooks and cost baselines.

- Objective C — Serving Reliability (Owner: Jonas Weber)
  - Key Result 1: 99.95% availability for hosted API across primary regions.
  - Key Result 2: Reduce tail latency (p95→p99) by 20% via kernel/serving changes.

Next steps
- Kimberly to submit privacy paragraph by Wed 12pm PT.
- Grace & Jonas to handoff runbooks to RevOps by Thu morning.
- Thu 3pm PT: 30m lock meeting (calendar invite sent). Final sign‑off will be captured in the meeting notes and the QBR packet will be shared with the Exec Review on Fri.

I’m marking this thread as the canonical sign‑off path — if anyone needs a separate escalation route, reply all and flag. Thanks all for quick turns.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
